//: Lighthouse CI budgets (family standard, same shape as the WCP repo). Used by .github/workflows/lighthouse.yml, a REAL gate: accessibility asserts as an error and must hold 100; performance / best-practices / SEO are warnings so normal CI variance never blocks a push. Runs against the built static output (dist/client) so dev-server quirks never affect scores. The url list is EXPLICIT on purpose: with staticDistDir alone, lhci auto-discovers pages but caps at 5, testing a near-random subset. It audits EVERY fixed route, the same list as tests/routes.ts; keep the two in sync when a fixed page ships. Dynamic [slug] detail routes are excluded: the CI empty-env build emits none. /studio, /preview and /api are Studio plumbing (SSR or noindex) and never belong here. Run locally: npm run build && npx lhci autorun (on Windows lhci can die on an EPERM temp-cleanup crash; see docs/TESTING.md).

assert.//: numberOfRuns is 3 and assertions use the MEDIAN, not a single sample. With one run, largest-contentful-paint as a hard error measures the CI runner as much as the site: on 2026-09-06 the identical commit passed on staging and failed on main at 6779ms against a 4500 budget, on a commit that only touched a workflow file. A gate that cries wolf gets ignored, and an ignored gate is worse than none. Three runs cost roughly 3x the job time, which is the price of the timing assertions being trustworthy.
